system.summary: Danish. 8-64 set: a homophonic table in four runs (14-27 k..y up, 28-37 k..a down, 38-49 a..m up, 50-61 z..n down), so most letters have two numbers; 8, 9, 10, 62, 63, 64 are nulls, mostly between words (63 and 64 also inside words); three-digit numbers are a nomenclator. The p. 115 passage is in Peder Vibe's old cipher (an opener sets a shift over a cyclic 23-letter alphabet). The p. 6 set (3-32) is unidentified.
system.notes: Open in the 8-64 table: 11, 12, 13 (no gloss); 50 stands where s is needed once, in a doubtful group (50|56) where the run gives z; in the build glosses 19 = t, 20 = s, 24 = o where the run would give p, q, u. The four runs are alphabetical, two upward and two downward.

prior_solution.where: Fryxell, Handlingar rörande Sverges historia 1 (1836) prints a Swedish abstract of this register without the cipher passages; DECODE, Tomokiyo and Lasry have nothing (catalogue vetting 11 Nov 2026); a web search of 12 Nov 2026 found nothing on these passages. Brice Dudout's PR #410 (vibejuel1651) publishes Vibe's old cipher and notes that p. 115 is in it, without reading it.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 2553) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, built and froze the key, ran the held-out test, read and checked. No human palaeographer checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (fetch, crops, decryption, held-out test, system tests, mark check)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), viewing the images

solution.what: Register images 5, 6, 7, 61 (unit 261585) and letters 115-135 (unit 261575) fetched at full size from api.rigsarkivet.dk, one at a time, 1.6 s apart.
Sign conventions written before any key; the register runs transcribed in two passes from fresh crops and reconciled on the image.
82 gloss pairs of images 117 and 121 (pairs_build.tsv); key frozen (key_frozen.tsv), unglossed values filled from the run pattern and marked.
Held-out image 118 (letter of 11 March 1648): 23 of 25 glossed numbers agree with the frozen key (0.92); 2000 permuted keys: mean 1.1, best 7 of 25. Image 118 had been looked at before the freeze.
Mechanical decryption and marked readings; scripts/check_marks.py passes on king, chancellor and vibe.
p. 6 (3-32 set): Vibe's old and new ciphers, the 8-64 table shifted by -40..+40, and plain rank ciphers tested; none gives Danish.
Collision check (open PRs, issues, targets and research on origin/main) and one web search; no prior decipherment found.

Blind review by an independent AI language-model agent: all cipher lines of pp. 5 and 115 copied from its own crops before the transcriptions were opened (about 153 of 156 and 147 of 150 numbers agree), decryptions, mark check and held-out test re-run, readings read as Danish. Grades B and B.

Fixes from the review's image readings: p. 115 line 4 14 -> 18 and 4 -> 8 (probable; 'bort', 'skal' now verbatim); p. 5 line 11 50 -> 56 ('holsten' verbatim); p. 5 line 2 marked 50|56 and line 10 33|53. Decryptions re-run; check_marks passes.
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 111 tokens, 39 types, da-modern order 4: reading -2.975 per letter; Verdict: too short.

texts.label: p. 5 top, to the King, 20 Nov 1647
texts.summary: Among them 83 and 84 would gladly have 124 as general in 158 again, but he cannot be persuaded.
texts.note: One short run (3 cipher words, all verbatim: 'til general i') inside clear Danish; four codes open.

texts.label: p. 5 entry No. 4, to the chancellor, 20 Nov 1647
texts.summary: A strong [war] council is held; they would gladly have 124 as general in 158; he could [...] become General of the Realm (Rigens Feltherre); something with Sparre and [quarters] in Holstein.
texts.note: 26 cipher words: 14 verbatim, 4 with a marked repair, 3 guesses, 5 holes (69% read). Checker clean share 0.571 on the plain reading. The last two sentences are mostly holes.

reading_review.note: Two of the four sentences hold as Danish (a strong war council is held and they would gladly have 124 as general in 158; he could become Rigens Feltherre); the last two cipher stretches are holes. Read in part is defensible here, not more.

texts.label: p. 6 entry No. 4, to Hannibal Sehested, 20 Nov 1647
texts.summary: Not solved: 30 numbers in a 3-32 set; no tested system gives Danish.
texts.note: The decryption file is the trial with Vibe's old cipher, which gives no Danish; the other tests are in scripts/test_332.py and work/test_332.out.

texts.label: p. 115, to Peder Vibe, 2 Sep 1648
texts.summary: 442 said some days ago to 212 that the former 412 of 351 277 [...] her away, and that 401 shall now bring her back; he drove for 412 of 426 with three wagons between.
texts.note: 25 cipher words: 23 verbatim, 1 guess, 1 hole. Nine codes are open and the clear text of the register between the runs is not transcribed, so the checker clean share is 0.333 on the plain reading.

reading_review.note: The cipher words read almost fully as Danish and the sense of the first sentence is clear: 442 said that the former 412 of 351 277 [...] her away and that 401 shall now bring her back. The holes are codes and untranscribed clear text, not failed decryption; the reviewer asked for that clear text to be transcribed.
